1.1 This standard covers the requirements for ball point pen refills made entirely from metal or metal and plastic materials. This does not cover jotter and special ball point pen refill where ceramic or ruby ball is used.
*Specification for ball point pens (Jirst revision ). ?Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 3

IS : 3707 - 1984

2. MATERIALS 2.1 Tube ( Ink Container ) - Tube shall be made of either any plastic or metal. When made of plastic, the material shall be sufficiently hard and rigid and shall have low moisture absorption. When made of metal, the material shall be rigid and shall have no visible defects or sharp edges.
2.2 Writing Tip - This shall be made from brass or nickel copper alloy or stainless steel or any other non-corrosive material having some hardness characteristic or higher than that of brass. 2.3 Ball - Ball shall be made of stainless steel or tungsten hardness of the ball shall be between 650 to 750 HV. carbide. The

2.4 Ink - The ink shall be solvent based. It shall contain no undissolved particles of dye or agglomerates of undispersed pigments. The ink shall be of such quality as to ensure a smooth and continuous writing. In all other respects the ink shall conform to IS : 5805-1970*. 3. DIMENSIONS shall be made according to dimensions given in Fig. 1 or Fig. 2 unless otherwise agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser. The diameter of the ball shall be between 0.50 to 1.20 mm as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. When refills of dimensions other than those given in Fig. 1 or Fig. 2 are ordered, they shall conform to all other provisions of this standard. 4. REQUIREMENTS

3.1 Refills

4.1 The

refill shall be so made as to be straight and concentric with its ball. The refills shall have either a collar or a crimping at a distance from the ball end as specified in Fig. 1 or 2. The refills shall be accurately made so that they are completely interchangeable with the ball point pens conforming to IS : 3705 19807, unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

4.2 The tube shall be filled with ink and shall not react with it. Colour The ink shall not of the ink shall normally be black, blue, green or red. overflow the barrel or leak around the baI1. The refill during disuse shall not ooze out ink when held with ball point tip upward and downward and shall not result in smudginess and discontinuity in writing. The ball shall be so mounted as to have free rotation to enable smooth The tip holding writing but shall not be loosely fitted nor loosen in use. the ball shall be worked over SO that its edge shall be smooth and not have any feathers, fins, etc, that would scratch the paper while writing.
*Specification $Specification for ball point pen ink. for ball point pens (first nvision ). 4

4.3jThe refill containing 0'3 g of ink shall write a continuous line of 1 000 m minimum for refill having ball diameter above 0.80 mm and 1 200 m minimum for refill having ball diameter up to 0.80 mm, when tested for length of writing as specified in 5.4.
5. TESTS of Writing ( Routine ) Test - Each refill shall be used to draw 50 to 60 continuous loops on a sheet of white supercalendered printing paper conforming to IS : 1848-1971* within a period of 15 seconds. The loops shall be continuous without excess deposit of ink and shall be uniform in colour. Writing shall be smooth and refill shall not scratch the paper. 5.1 Smoothness

5.2 Writing Characteristics ( Type ) Test - The refill shall $be tested on a sheet of white super-calendered printing paper or cream laid or cream wove paper conforming to IS : 1848-1971* by writing numerous fast as well as slow letters, flourishes, ovals, reversals, angles, etc. The writing shall be such that it has complete continuity without excess deposit of ink or variation in intensity or line getting split up. 5.3 Starting Test - The refill shall be made to draw a few lines or letters on a sheet of paper to ensure continuous writing. The refill shall then be kept in the vertical position with the writing tip upward for The refill shall now be tested on a white super-calendered 30 minutes. printing paper or cream laid or cream wove paper conforming to IS : 1848-1971* by drawing at least four lines, starting exactly from the The refill shall start marking the margin, with normal writing pressure. first line from a distance of not more than 15 mm and the subsequent line shall start immediately from the margin where they are drawn.
*Specification for writing and printing papers ( jirst revision ).

5.4.1 Apparatus a) Standard Paper - The paper shall be white super-calendered printing paper or cream laid or cream wove paper conforming to IS : 1848-1971*.

b) Standard

writing machine designed Test Machine - A mechanical to give continuous writing while rotating the pens simultaneously: 1) on their axis, and 2) with speed setting of 110 mm/set.

The pens shall be fixed in such a way that they move freely up and down in their holders at a writing pressure of 125 f 2 grams. The acute angle between the paper and the pens shall be 80 f 2 degrees. A paperfeed mechanism shall feed the rolled paper automatically through the A revolution counter indicating the number of metres test machine. written during the test shall be fitted. the protective coating, if any, from 5.4.2 Writing Test - Remove Write lines and turns by hand with the balls of the refills under test. each test sample until writing commences. Place the pens in the standard Stop the machine after each test machine and start the writing test. 500 metres of writing and, using a clean cloth, remove accumulated ink Mark the standard paper at and paper dust from the writing tips. points along its length to indicate each 500 metres of writing. Continue the test until each test sample ceases to write a continuous line. Reserve the test papers for assessment of length and continuity of writing. Any adjustment in the interruption of continuity due to any necessary mechanism or change of paper rolls shall be neglected. 5.5 Smearing Test - After writing a few lines or letters on a sheet of white super-calendered printing paper or cream laid or cream wove paper conforming to IS : 1848-1971" and waiting for 5 seconds, the writing shall The ink shall have been dried, so that it be rubbed lightly with hand. Further there shall be no feathering or spreading could not be smeared. or strike through the paper. 5.6 Test for Resistance to Water - Ten different letters shall be written with the refill on a sheet of cream laid or cream wove paper The paper shall then be immersed in conforming to IS : 1848-l 97 1*. The paper water maintained at a temperature 25 &- 2�C for 24 hours. shall then be removed and allowed to dry and then be examined. The letters shall remain legible. *Specification for writing and printing papers (Jirst revision).

IS : 3707 - 1984 5.7 Corrosion Resistance Test - The metal parts of the refill shall be dipped in a boiling 10 percent ( w/ret) aqueous solution of sodium After removal from this solution chloride for a period of 15 minutes. they shall be immersed in 10 percent ( w/W ) aqueous solution of sodium chloride at room temperature for 2 hours. They shall then be removed, washed with clean water, wiped with a soft cloth and allowed to dry for 24 hours at room temperature. Th e metal parts shall not show any visible signs 6f corrosion. 5.8 Accelerated Ageing Test - The refills shall be suspended down and subjected successively to each of the following conditions: Exposure I II Time ( Hours ) 168 48 Temperature 60 f -2 f 1�C 1�C point

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that Details of conditions, under which a licence for the. standard as a further safeguard. use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors,, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

In any consignment, all' the ball point pen refiIls manufactured under similar conditions, from the same raw materials and of same dimensions shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.

IS : 3707 - 1984 A-2.2 The refills in the sample shall be selected at random from the lot and in order to ensure the randomness of selection, IS : 4905-1968* may be used. A-3. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

A-3.1 The refills selected according to A-2.1 and A-2.2 shall be inspected for dimensions ( 3.1 ) and requirements ( 4.1 to 4.3 ). The refill failing in any one or more of the requirements shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the above requirements if the number of defective refills in the sample does not exceed the number given in co1 3 of Table 1. A-3.2 The lot having been found conforming to A-3.1 shall be tested for smoothness of writing test ( 5.1 ), writing characteristics test ( 5.2 ), strating test ( 5.3 ), length of writing ( 5.4 ), smearing test ( 5.5 ) and test for resistance to water ( 5.6 ), For this purpose, a sub-sample of size given in co1 4 of Table 1 shall be taken from the refills selected as in A-2.1 and A-2.2. Each of the refills in the sub-sample shall be subjected to the test mentioned above. A refill failing in one or more of the tests shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the above-mentioned requirements if the number of defectives in the sub-sample does not exceed the number given in co1 5 of Table 1. A-3.3 The lot having been found conforming to A-3.2, a sample of refills shall be tested for corrosion resistance test ( 5.7 ) and accelerated ageing test (5.8 ). A refill failing in any one of the tests shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of the tests if the sample passes both the tests. A-3.4 The lot shall be accepted if A-3.1, A-3.2 and A-3.3 are satisfied.
